bull_bear.body:
- 23-year-old brand in aesthetic dermatology, having served over 35 lakh customers with personalised solutions
- One of India's foremost networks of expert dermatologists - 120+ dermatologists across 80+ clinics and 600+ service lines
- Doctor-first philosophy: in-house expert dermatologists design and formulate all services and products, supporting safety, efficacy and trusted outcomes
- Integrated clinic-plus-product model - clinical expertise extends into a skincare product portfolio with research-rooted formulations, giving recurring consumption alongside treatments
- Access to globally approved technologies and scientifically backed procedures, with technology-enabled diagnostics and advanced treatment protocols
- Customer base engagement through the Kaya Smiles loyalty programme with 100K+ members
- Skilled, largely women workforce (85%+ women) of dermatologists, therapists and clinic teams delivering personalised care
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Shifts in consumer behaviour — Explicitly tracked by management as a key external risk factor. Kaya's demand is discretionary, consumer-led aesthetic care, and the MD&A itself describes rapidly changing consumer mindsets - the move to preventive and personalised regimes, premiumisation and digital-led discovery - so a change in consumer preference directly affects clinic footfall and treatment mix.
- Increasing competitive intensity — Explicitly tracked by management. The MD&A notes the industry is transitioning to a more organised, technology-driven and experience-led ecosystem in which differentiation will be driven by clinical credibility, innovation and customer engagement, and that players integrating advanced technologies with personalised care and strong brand positioning are likely to capture disproportionate value - implying share loss risk for those who do not.
- Technological disruption — Explicitly tracked by management. Treatment outcomes in aesthetic dermatology depend on device and protocol technology (laser platforms, energy-based devices, regenerative and diagnostic systems); continuous technology refresh is required to stay competitive, making the business exposed to obsolescence of installed clinical platforms.
- Regulatory developments — Explicitly tracked by management, with the risk framework designed to ensure alignment with evolving regulatory requirements. Kaya operates medically supervised clinical procedures and sells dermatology-linked products, both of which sit in regulated territory.
- Dependence on continuous clinical innovation and protocol adoption to sustain positioning — Management states the Company aims to scale leadership by continuously enhancing service offerings and strengthening technology capabilities; its stated competitive position rests on advanced technology adoption (for example Aerolase, MCT and Artiqa platforms) and standardised protocols, so a lag in adoption would erode the differentiation the strategy relies on.

business.body: Kaya Limited operates a dermatologist-led network of skin, hair and body care clinics in India, combining clinical expertise with globally approved technologies and scientifically backed procedures to deliver personalised treatments. Alongside in-clinic services such as anti-ageing, acne and scars, brightening and pigmentation, laser hair reduction, hair care and body contouring, the Company sells a range of dermatologist-formulated skincare, haircare, bath-and-body and nutraceutical products that extend clinical benefits into daily consumer routines. Its in-house dermatologists design and formulate all services and products, and the business is supported by technology-enabled diagnostics, standardised treatment protocols and a customer-centric, doctor-first operating philosophy.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the omnichannel ecosystem across clinics and digital channels, making expert dermatology more accessible, personalised and seamless
- Deepen investments in cutting-edge dermatology technologies and digital healthcare solutions, including advanced diagnostics, skin analysis and treatment planning
- Expand the clinic network across high-potential markets, alongside strategic relocations and infrastructure upgrades of existing clinics
- Accelerate innovation across products, services and customer engagement platforms, with launches spanning hair care, anti-ageing, nutraceuticals, sun care and post-treatment recovery
- Deploy advanced dermatological technologies across the network - additions during FY26 included Aerolase, MCT for Hair and Artiqa - to widen the specialised treatment portfolio
- Reinforce a doctor-first, science-backed brand positioning through targeted digital campaigns, hyperlocal outreach, dermatologist-led education and lifestyle partnerships
- Strengthen digital customer engagement and appointment management - automated reminders, follow-ups and visit confirmations - to reduce no-shows and improve service continuity
- Invest in capability building, continuous learning and leadership development for dermatologists, therapists and clinic teams
- The Board did not recommend any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. Equity was raised during the year through a preferential issue of 20,90,068 equity shares to Axana Estates LLP on August 12, 2025, leaving paid-up equity capital of 1,51,87,609 shares of `10 each as on March 31, 2026. A transfer was made to general reserve from the share options outstanding account. The Company accepted no public deposits during the year and reported no one-time settlement with banks or financial institutions, no proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and no change in the nature of its business operations. Employee incentives are delivered through the Kaya ESOP 2016 and Kaya ESOP 2021 plans, the latter amended during the year to permit the grant of Restricted Stock Units.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Kaya's expansion is footprint- and technology-led rather than plant-based: the Company operates a network of 120+ dermatologists, 80+ clinics and over 600 service lines with an omnichannel presence across 26 cities and 15 states. During FY26 it continued to strengthen the clinic network through new clinic launches, strategic relocations and infrastructure upgrades aimed at enhancing accessibility, convenience and customer experience, and it expanded and upgraded the network alongside the introduction of advanced technologies and innovative products. Management states it accelerated investments during the year in advanced dermatology platforms, diagnostics, digital engagement, clinic infrastructure, and innovation-led products and services, together with technology integration, network enhancement, branding and capability-building initiatives, describing these as building the foundation for sustainable long-term growth. The product footprint was also widened, with 75+ product offerings in FY26. On the funding side, the Company issued 20,90,068 equity shares on August 12, 2025 to Axana Estates LLP pursuant to a preferential issue. No rupee capex outlay, commissioning schedule, clinic-addition target or dated expansion project is disclosed in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management states Kaya remains well-positioned to capitalise on favourable demand trends, supported by clinical expertise, a trusted brand and expanding consumer engagement across both physical and digital channels
- Services remained the primary contributor at 84% of clinic business in FY26, with growth across anti-ageing, acne and scars, pigmentation management, hair care and body contouring; products contributed 16% of clinic collections
- Acne and scars treatments recorded strong growth, while brightening and pigmentation solutions continued to see encouraging momentum
- India's aesthetic services market estimated at `5,193 crore in FY26 and projected to reach `7,540 crore by FY29, a CAGR of 13.3%, with growth broad-based across skin, body and hair treatments
- Skin treatments are the largest segment at 43.2% of the market, body at 31.2% and hair at 25.6%; North India is the largest region at 32.4%
- Rising income levels, urbanisation and a growing middle class expected to accelerate discretionary spending across wellness and lifestyle categories; PFCE accounts for over 60% of India's GDP
- Digital adoption, increasing penetration of organised healthcare services and heightened consumer awareness around appearance and self-care expected to drive long-term growth in aesthetic dermatology
- Shift from reactive treatment to preventive, maintenance-led skincare expands the addressable market beyond clinical intervention and enables recurring consumption and higher customer lifetime value
- Growing preference for non-invasive and minimally invasive procedures - lasers, skin rejuvenation, energy-based treatments - is the key growth engine for cosmetic dermatology
- Transition of products from prescription to OTC/OTx consumer-accessible formats unlocks scale and wider penetration
- Deeper penetration into Tier II and Tier III cities and India's emergence as a medical tourism destination broaden the demand base
- Increasing formalisation and consolidation of the market expected to favour organised, science-led players with differentiated technologies and integrated care models
- Near-term watch-items: IMF sees global growth moderating from 3.4% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026, with geopolitical tensions, elevated energy and commodity prices and financial market volatility weighing on activity
